title: Files, Config Projection, And Reload
objective: Move filesystem and config behavior behind Server V2 by implementing server-owned file APIs, config projection into OpenCode, reload events, and reconciliation of managed config state.

steps.name: Define the config materialization service
steps.description: Create the service boundary that computes effective OpenWork and OpenCode config for a workspace from server-owned DB state and linking tables.
successFactors: Config projection is computed in one place.
Later routes can ask for effective workspace config without duplicating logic.
The service reflects the ownership model in `ideal-flow.md` and `schema.md`.

steps.name: Implement workspace config directory creation
steps.description: Ensure each local workspace gets a server-owned config directory separate from the user-selected data directory so OpenWork and OpenCode state can be managed cleanly.
successFactors: Local workspaces have separate `data_dir` and `config_dir` semantics.
The path shape aligns with `workspaces/<workspaceId>/config` or the chosen equivalent.
Later config projection can write into a predictable location.

steps.name: Implement local workspace creation on Server V2
steps.description: Move local workspace creation into Server V2 so directory creation, config directory setup, ID assignment, and initial registry updates are server-owned.
successFactors: The server can create a local workspace end to end.
Workspace creation updates the registry and filesystem consistently.
The app or Tauri layer no longer needs to own the durable creation logic.

steps.name: Materialize authorized roots and workspace paths
steps.description: Implement the rules that add the user data directory as an authorized path and project any other OpenWork-managed root or workspace path settings into effective config.
successFactors: Authorized roots are generated from server-owned state.
Workspace data and config paths are reflected correctly in materialized config.
The rules do not require direct Tauri file editing to stay consistent.

steps.name: Implement config read routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 routes for reading effective or raw OpenWork/OpenCode config so settings UIs can stop reading config directly from local files.
successFactors: Config reads are routed through Server V2.
The server can return effective config and raw/editable config where needed.
Response shapes make it clear what is materialized versus stored.

steps.name: Implement config patch and write routes
steps.description: Add the server-owned mutation routes for config changes, including audit logging and any reload or projection follow-up that should happen after a write.
successFactors: Config mutation no longer relies on direct app or Tauri writes for migrated flows.
Writes go through one audit-aware server path.
Resulting config state is reflected in the DB and materialized files consistently.

steps.name: Implement OpenCode config projection
steps.description: Project server-owned config items and workspace settings into the OpenCode config object or file shape needed by the runtime, without making those files the source of truth.
successFactors: OpenCode receives the effective config it needs.
The server DB remains the source of truth for managed concepts.
Projection logic supports later managed-item phases without redesign.

steps.name: Implement the file-session store or equivalent
steps.description: Port or redesign the file-session model so the server can manage scoped file editing sessions, catalogs, cursors, and conflict detection inside Server V2.
successFactors: The server owns file editing session state.
The model supports conflict detection and incremental events.
The implementation is isolated from legacy server globals.

steps.name: Implement file-session create and catalog routes
steps.description: Add the routes that create a file session and return the workspace file catalog snapshot needed by editors or remote file-management tooling.
successFactors: Clients can start a file session through Server V2.
Catalog responses include the data needed by migrated editors.
The routes follow the shared auth and error model.

steps.name: Implement file read and write routes
steps.description: Add the scoped file read and write routes with conflict detection and audit/reload behavior so workspace file editing is clearly server-owned.
successFactors: The server can read and write workspace files through the file-session model.
Writes detect stale revisions or conflicting edits where required.
The resulting mutations trigger the correct audit and reload flows.

steps.name: Implement mkdir, rename, and delete routes
steps.description: Add the remaining file operation routes needed for practical workspace file management through Server V2.
successFactors: Create, rename, and delete operations exist under the server boundary.
Operation failures use consistent typed errors.
The file-event or reload model sees these changes too.

steps.name: Implement simple content routes
steps.description: Add the lighter markdown or simple-content read/write routes used by simpler document flows so those paths do not remain on legacy file mutation APIs.
successFactors: Simple document editing can use Server V2.
The routes are consistent with the rest of the server-owned file model.
The app can migrate lighter file flows without needing the full file-session API.

steps.name: Implement inbox and outbox routes
steps.description: Add uploadable inbox and downloadable artifact routes under Server V2 for file ingest and artifact retrieval workflows.
successFactors: The server can accept uploaded files into the managed workspace area.
Artifact download flows are served by Server V2.
The routes respect workspace scoping and auth rules.

steps.name: Implement the reload event store
steps.description: Port or redesign the reload event queue so Server V2 can publish workspace-scoped reload signals after config or file mutations and after watched filesystem changes.
successFactors: Workspace-scoped reload events are stored and queryable.
Server-caused mutations emit explicit reload signals.
The behavior matches the queueing and workspace isolation principles in the broader docs.

steps.name: Implement managed file watching
steps.description: Add file watching over managed config directories and any required workspace paths so the server can detect out-of-band changes and queue reload or reconciliation work.
successFactors: The server watches the intended directories only.
Watcher output feeds reload or reconciliation logic cleanly.
Watch behavior does not recreate the old app-owned watcher model.

steps.name: Implement startup reconciliation and periodic repair
steps.description: Add the repair path that reconciles DB state with managed files on startup or periodic checks so missed watcher events do not leave the system inconsistent.
successFactors: The server can recover from missed file events.
Startup repair is idempotent and observable.
Disk and DB state can be brought back into alignment safely.

steps.name: Implement config absorption for recognized items
steps.description: Detect recognized unmanaged files in the workspace config directory and absorb them into managed DB records while leaving unknown files in place.
successFactors: Recognized MCP, skill, plugin, or provider shapes can be imported automatically.
Unknown manual files are left alone.
Absorption behavior is explicit and testable.

steps.name: Implement explicit engine reload if still required
steps.description: If the product still needs a manual engine reload route during migration, add it under the new namespace and make it call the new runtime supervisor instead of legacy proxy code.
successFactors: Manual reload, if kept, is owned by Server V2.
The route is not a thin proxy to legacy server internals.
Reload semantics are consistent with the runtime supervisor.

steps.name: Migrate config and file UI surfaces
steps.description: Move the app and any remaining Tauri-backed config or file flows onto Server V2 for the migrated areas so direct local mutation becomes fallback-only debt instead of a primary path.
successFactors: Migrated settings and file flows go through Server V2.
Direct Tauri or app-local file mutation is reduced for covered slices.
Legacy fallbacks remain quarantined and deletable.

steps.name: Add file and config tests
steps.description: Write tests for file session behavior, conflict handling, reload events, config projection, absorption, and reconciliation so these ownership-heavy flows are guarded before later cleanup phases.
successFactors: Critical file and config behaviors are covered by automated tests.
Conflict and reload edge cases are asserted explicitly.
The tests prove the server, not the UI, owns the migrated workspace mutation paths.
